observation_method: Native view of complete original folio; no crop, OCR, synthetic reconstruction or translated-image substitution.
observations: Green vertical central trunk shaped as a cross, with twelve curving inscribed branch ribbons, six on each side.
One heart-shaped inner label hangs from each branch. These twelve units differ from the outer three-lobed scripture citation units.
Branches visibly carry repeated IHC initial groups with four short clause slots on each branch. This is a layout observation; not all48 clauses have been diplomatically collated here.
A central basal three-lobed unit identifies Johannes in apoc.xxii and describes twelve fruits and medicinal leaves; it is not a thirteenth ingredient.
The top central figure is a bird bending toward young in a nest. The pelican name occurs beside it; this is an additional metaphorical image, not a botanical organ assembled from another plant.

Bottom left inner fruit reads Preclaritas originis; bottom right Humilitas conversationis. Upper inner units include resurrectionis novitas, ascensionis sublimitas, equitas iudicii and eternitas regni.
Outer bottom-right scripture citations and top bird add interpretive material beyond the twelve heart-labelled branches. They must not be flattened into one uniform node class.
uncertainties: The complete prologue is supplied from a separately hosted Latin edition, not transcribed from this diagram. No claim that MS416 contains that full prologue.
All48 branch clauses and all marginal citations have not been collated; no exact overall label count beyond the clearly visible12 branch/heart pairs is certified.
Different manuscript diagrams can change wording or arrangement. This witness does not establish a universal medieval diagram grammar.
No instruction here assembles anatomical parts from different real plants or maps a botanical composite to recipe ingredients.
